candidates.label: mainContentOfPage
candidates.comment: A main content relation between a web page and the web page element that constitutes its primary subject. Also called: primary content, central element, core content. Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage
candidates.comment: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: primaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: coach
candidates.comment: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: numberOfEpisodes

candidates.label: numTracks

candidates.label: numberOfSeasons
candidates.comment: The total number of seasons within a radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called season count, series seasons, total seasons. candidates.label: repeatCount

Examples: "A weekly meeting schedule has a repeat count of 10.", "A training course schedule has a repeat count of 5.", "A daily alarm schedule has a repeat count of 365."

candidates.label: answerCount
candidates.comment: An answer count relation between a question and the total number of answers it has received. Also called number of responses, reply count, solution count. Examples: "A forum question's answer count is '5'.", "The quiz question's answer count is '10'."

candidates.label: remainingAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A remaining attendee capacity relation between an event and the number of available spots for attendees. Also called available seats, remaining tickets, open spots. Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."

candidates.label: ticketNumber
candidates.comment: A unique textual identifier for a ticket. Also called "ticket ID", "booking number", "reference number", "ticket code". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketNumber 'ABC123XYZ'", "The flight ticket's ticketNumber is a unique alphanumeric code", "This ticket is identified by its ticketNumber."

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: bestRating
candidates.comment: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: totalHistoricalEnrollment
candidates.comment: A total historical enrollment relation between a course and the cumulative number of students who have ever enrolled in it. Also called cumulative enrollment, past enrollment count, historical student count. Examples: "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '500'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '1200'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '75'".

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: upvoteCount
candidates.comment: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".

candidates.label: cvdNumICUBeds
candidates.comment: A capacity relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of staffed inpatient intensive care unit (ICU) beds. Also called: total ICU beds, ICU bed count, intensive care capacity. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num icu beds "50", "Facility B Report" cvd num icu beds "20", "Medical Center C" cvd num icu beds "100". Distinct from cvdNumICUBedsOcc, which is the number of occupied ICU beds.

candidates.label: annualPercentageRate

Also called APR, yearly interest rate, effective annual rate. Examples: "A loan's annual percentage rate is '5.99%'.", "The credit card's annual percentage rate is '18.5%'."

candidates.label: interestRate

Examples: A savings account has an interestRate of '0.5%'. A loan has an interestRate of '4.99%'. A bond has an interestRate of '3.2% fixed'. Distinct from annualPercentageRate, which is the total cost of borrowing over a year, including fees.

candidates.label: percentile90
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 90th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 90th percentage point, upper decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile90 of 90. The data shows a percentile90 of 45.5. The scores have a percentile90 of 95.

candidates.label: percentile10
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 10th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 10th percentage point, lower decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile10 of 10. The data shows a percentile10 of 5.5. The scores have a percentile10 of 60.

candidates.label: percentile25
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 25th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 25th percentage point, first quartile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile25 of 25. The data shows a percentile25 of 12.5. The scores have a percentile25 of 70.

candidates.label: percentile75
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 75th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 75th percentage point, third quartile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile75 of 75. The data shows a percentile75 of 37.5. The scores have a percentile75 of 90.

candidates.label: healthPlanCoinsuranceRate
candidates.comment: A coinsurance rate relation between a health plan cost-sharing specification and the numerical rate of coinsurance. Also called coinsurance percentage, rate of coinsurance, coinsurance ratio. Examples: "Health plan cost-sharing has a coinsurance rate of 0.2.", "The specification includes a coinsurance rate of 0.15.", "This plan's coinsurance rate is 0.3."

candidates.label: orderPercentage
candidates.comment: A percentage value representing the fraction of the total order value charged as shipping cost. Also called shipping cost percentage, freight percentage, delivery fee rate. Examples: "Standard Shipping orderPercentage 0.05", "Express Shipping orderPercentage 0.10", "International Shipping orderPercentage 0.15". Distinct from shippingSettingsLink, which is a URL to shipping information.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: weightPercentage
candidates.comment: A fractional weight contribution relation between shipping rate settings and a numerical value, indicating the proportion of weight used for price calculation. Also called weight fraction, weight ratio, weight factor, weight proportion. Examples: ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.10, ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.05, ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.25.

candidates.label: totalPrice
candidates.comment: A total price relation between a reservation or ticket and its full cost, including taxes and shipping. Also called full cost, final price, reservation cost. Examples: "Reservation totalPrice '$120.00'", "Ticket totalPrice '€50.00'", "Flight reservation totalPrice '$350.75'".

candidates.label: offerCount

Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: totalHistoricalEnrollment
candidates.comment: A total historical enrollment relation between a course and the cumulative number of students who have ever enrolled in it. Also called cumulative enrollment, past enrollment count, historical student count. Examples: "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '500'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '1200'", "Course totalHistoricalEnrollment '75'".

candidates.label: hasShippingService
candidates.comment: A shipping service relation between offer shipping details or an organization and a shipping service it provides. Also called offers shipping, shipping option, delivery service. candidates.label: numberOfBathroomsTotal
candidates.comment: The total integer count of all bathrooms (full, three-quarter, and half) within an accommodation or floor plan. Also called total bathroom count, bathroom total, sum of bathrooms. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfBathroomsTotal 2", "House B numberOfBathroomsTotal 3", "Hotel Room C numberOfBathroomsTotal 1". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms and numberOfPartialBathrooms, which specify specific types of bathrooms.

candidates.label: hasMerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: A merchant return policy relation between an offer, organization, or product and its applicable return policy. Also called return policy, refund policy, returns information. Examples: "A product has a merchant return policy of 30 days.", "An organization has a merchant return policy for all sales.", "The offer includes a merchant return policy."

candidates.label: isProprietary

candidates.label: workPresented

candidates.label: actor

Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries

Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: hasShippingService

candidates.label: hasMemberProgram

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog

Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: iso6523Code

candidates.label: isrcCode

candidates.label: hasGS1DigitalLink

candidates.label: isbn

candidates.label: hasTierBenefit
candidates.comment: A tier benefit relation between a member program tier and a specific benefit associated with that tier. Also called tier advantage, member perk, program benefit. Examples: "A loyalty program tier has a tier benefit of free shipping.", "The premium tier has a tier benefit of exclusive access.", "This tier offers a tier benefit of bonus points."
